A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RQNN architecture and universality results. The complete documents are readable, including v2's Appendices A–E. Proofs moved from v1's main text can be matched to v2's appendices.

before.justification: v1 presents mathematical constructions, approximation bounds and proofs. Experimental applications are attributed to cited work; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its new circuit schematic, construction example and Monte Carlo error bounds do not report experiments, simulations or measured outcomes.

M1.justification: The U/V circuit, probability-based recurrent update, linear readout and preprocessing-matrix construction are retained. The explicit construction of V and sampling discussion elaborate the existing procedure; corrected normalization factors repair its mathematical description.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmark tasks. Applications mentioned in the literature discussion are not evaluations performed by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. v2's comparison with Gonon et al. (2023) concerns theoretical approximation assumptions, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols are reported in either version. The symbolic shot count S in Appendix E supports a theoretical derivation rather than specifying a conducted experiment or revised evaluation budget.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an analytical study of finite-shot measurement error and its propagation through recurrent feedback, including conditional uniform-error control and an expected-error bound. v1 only referred externally to controlled Monte Carlo error. This is supplementary error analysis, without experimental robustness tests.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly defines the empirical-frequency estimator for S independent shots and quantifies sampling uncertainty through variance calculations and inverse-square-root shot-count bounds. v1 supplied only a reference to Monte Carlo error control. This adds theoretical uncertainty quantification, not reported experimental runs, seeds or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured scores, empirical rankings or experimental result entries. The added symbolic approximation and sampling-error guarantees are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 2.7's componentwise condition ||∇x Fj|| ≤ λ/√N becomes the weaker spectral-norm condition ||∇x F||₂ ≤ λ in v2 Theorem 4.6, with a revised proof. v2 also supplies a full output-representation proof, corrects missing circuit normalization factors, and derives finite-shot bounds in Appendix E. Its newly added exact qubit-count identity, however, conflicts with the stated circuit dimension.

C1.justification: Linear-readout universality and approximation of state-space systems remain the central contributions. v2's abstract and contribution list additionally make explicit resource-efficiency claims: dimension-independent approximation-rate exponents and logarithmic qubit growth with inverse accuracy, drawing on the retained approximation rate.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the approximation theorem as offering weaker smoothness requirements than a classical RNN result. It also discusses rough or noncontractive targets, training difficulties and barren plateaus, and the continuity caveat for uniform finite-shot bounds. The existing distinction between trainable variational circuits and randomized reservoirs remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies an explicit reflection-based construction of V where v1 largely referred elsewhere. v2 also explains circuit initialization, measurement and feedback more explicitly and documents the sampling estimator and independence assumptions. No concrete experimental hyperparameters, hardware runs or new code release are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially expands positioning within classical and feedforward quantum approximation literature, including Hornik, Pérez-Salinas et al., Yu et al., and Aftab and Yang. Section 4.2 adds an explicit claimed smoothness advantage over Gonon et al. (2023), while new training, barren-plateau and sampling-error references broaden the discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with separate related-literature and contribution subsections. Background and architecture become standalone sections; the earlier protocol discussion moves to Appendix A and most proofs move to Appendices B–C. The contents page is removed and explanatory transitions are expanded.

P2.justification: v2 introduces document-wide changes to typography, heading and author styles, headers and equation layout. It also adds Figure 1, a circuit-and-feedback schematic absent from v1. Neither version contains result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 is more accessible and self-contained through its reorganized exposition, explicit circuit derivation and construction, and finite-shot analysis. The weaker contraction assumption also broadens the retained approximation theorem. These gains are tempered by a new error in Section 3: ceil(log2(2n)) undercounts by one qubit relative to the stated 4n+n0 circuit dimension, although the logarithmic scaling claim survives.
